profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
Software Engineer with 10+ years of experience in the tech industry.

I first entered the tech industry when a startup called Locket offered me a job after I reported security vulnerabilities to them (via white-hat hacking). I joined Locket as the 2nd engineer on the team and worked on its Android lockscreen app, which was considered one of the "Best Apps of 2014" by Google Play, had investments from Tyra Banks, and was acquired by Wish in 2015.

After the acquisition of Locket, I took a gap year working on my own projects, achieved an Android Developer Nanodegree from Udacity, and came in 4th place at the Salesforce $1 Million Hackathon. I spent some time analyzing the security of various apps including Instagram and wrote a few technical Medium articles detailing my findings. One of my favorite accomplishments from then is building Chrome IG Story, a Google Chrome extension that allowed you to watch Instagram Stories on your computer before Instagram implemented the functionality themselves. The extension was covered by various tech blogs, had over 1 million users, and was live for 2.5 years before Facebook sent me a Cease & Desist letter to take it down. 

After my gap year I joined a startup called Youplus where I lead the design and implementation of multiple Android and web products for 3.5 years until the company ran out of funding and shut down in January 2020.

I spent the pandemic interviewing at various tech companies and working on my portfolio. I ended up building an open source web app for Byte (byte.co, which has since been shut down), an app that had been recently launched at the time to compete with TikTok. I reverse engineered Byte’s private APIs to provide a web experience that seamlessly emulated the mobile app. You can read about my process building the web app in my Medium article: https://betterprogramming.pub/how-i-reverse-engineered-byte-and-created-my-own-byte-web-app-2828f5520b25?sk=28f57dea628b974b3e12c558aaf64bda

In March 2021 I landed an offer from Google and joined the Google.org team which is the philanthropy arm of Google that provides programs for underserved communities. My core work was supporting Google for Nonprofits, an offering that provides nonprofit organizations free or discounted access to Google products such as Ad Grants, Workspace, and YouTube Giving features. Learn more: google.com/nonprofits

In March 2024 I joined the Android Security team at Google.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Currently working on Android Security. Previously supported Google.org and Google for Nonprofits (G4NP).

positions.title: Front-End Software Engineer
positions.description:
• After the company pivoted and shut down the Android app I transitioned to Frontend work and started developing Youplus' web apps (React.js) as the company's only Frontend Engineer at the time.

• Developed numerous internal web dashboards and client-facing web products:

- VOCAL: platform that allowed consumers to give feedback to brands via video.
   * owned the work for both the user portal and admin dashboard
   * the user portal allowed for answering questions by recording a video (using WebRTC) or through a series of dynamic forms such as radio, checkbox, and text input.
   * the admin dashboard allowed for partners to create and manage their case studies and view video responses from users.

- VISION: a more advanced version of VOCAL's admin dashboard that showed realtime data for the videos analyzed by our AI.
   * Worked on displaying different charts and graphs that would visualize attributes such as facial sentiment and tonal analysis for the video that is currently playing.

- VIEW: widget that our clients could embed on their websites that would display a carousel of relevant videos to increase site engagement. For example, on e-commerce websites the widget would show relevant product review videos.
   * Contributed to the development of different types of widget designs and functionalities. 

• Traveled to India every other month to collaborate with the team because I was the remaining US employee besides the CEO and the entire company was based in Bangalore.

positions.title: Android Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Joined as the only Android Engineer in the company and worked on the Youplus Android app.

 - The original Youplus app showed offers from nearby merchants for free samples (coffee, sandwich, etc.). I implemented a map view for offers and a system for users to give feedback on sponsored offers in exchange for monetary rewards before the app pivoted.
 - The app pivoted to a video opinion based social network and I implemented camera support to allow users to record their opinions on trending news articles and other users could explore other people's opinions in an Instagram-stories-like interface.

• Developed another Android app called Mic in parallel while working on the company's web apps.

- Mic was an app that allowed members of our opinion panels to record a short video and express their opinion on various case studies that our clients would create. The videos were then processed by our AI to extract insights such as sentiment.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Worked closely with the small team on the Android client logic and UI.
• Responsible for development of products, putting in long hours and tirelessly coding until the last bug was squashed on release day, never losing focus until the release button was pressed.
• Locket was selected as one of the "Best Apps of 2014" by Google, and acquired by mobile shopping app Wish in 2015.

positions.title: Locket Lab Intern
positions.description:
• Developed production code as an intern alongside the only other developer at the time, working 18hrs/day, and was promoted to a full-time Software Engineer after 7 months.
• When Locket first launched, I decompiled their app and found their server endpoints hardcoded in the source. I was curious, so I experimented with the endpoints and found a couple security vulnerabilities in their server.
• Immediately notified Locket at their New York office about vulnerabilities and they were so impressed they offered me a summer internship. A few months later I left college in my sophomore year because they decided to open a San Francisco office and I was invited to help establish it.

positions.title: Team Member, Team 3027 Seraphim Systems
positions.description: • Helped design, manufacture, program, and troubleshoot a robot designed to compete in annual challenges created by FIRST Robotics.

projects.title: Byte Community (Unofficial)
projects.description:
Immerse yourself in the Byte universe: an exciting new looping video app from the founder of Vine.
Explore, watch, and share bytes on the web.

I reverse engineered the APIs used in Byte's mobile apps and created an unofficial web app that lets users anonymous explore and watch bytes or if they login they can access their personalized home feed, like and comment on videos, and follow users.

Open Source on GitHub: https://github.com/CaliAlec/Byte-Community

Read my article to learn how I did it: https://medium.com/@calialec/how-i-reverse-engineered-byte-and-created-my-own-byte-web-app-2828f5520b25

projects.title: Insta360 Community (Unofficial)
projects.description:
Immerse yourself in fullscreen 360° panoramas and other content shared by photographers using Insta360's line of 360° cameras.

I reverse engineered the APIs used in Insta360 mobile apps and created an unofficial web app that ports the community for sharing 360° content captured by Insta360 cameras that already exists inside the apps.

Open Source on GitHub: https://github.com/CaliAlec/Insta360-Community
